title: iLBC: fix deprecation type and cast.
description:
In latest libilbc (3.0.3) the type iLBC_decinst_t has been marked
deprecated.
Other fixes rely on function prototype requiring uint8_t pointer.

Hey @geraldcombs, why is the windows job running on this MR? I cannot find another one that triggers it, and I don't get why it's failing.

Hi Dario,

It fails because the change is not correct as it does not consider previous versions of the iLBC library (2.0.2 for Windows). Search for ilbc string in the log to see the numerous errors the changes trigger.
Thanks. That answers my second point. The first still remains: why the window jobs runs for this MR only? I can't find another one with the same job, but may be it's just me.

> why the window jobs runs for this MR only?

We _might_ be able to build Wireshark on Windows using GitLab's shared runners, but it would require installing a bunch of dependencies each run, including Perl and Qt. Instead, the merge-req:windows job uses a [specific runner](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/runners/#specific-runners) linked to wireshark/wireshark which can run [our own Docker image](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark-containers/-/tree/master/dev/windows). Unfortunately I haven't been able to figure out how to get it to work with pipeline jobs [run from forks](https://gitlab.com/moshekaplan/wireshark/-/pipelines/233420331).
It works now.

Do we try to compile this code without having iLBC installed? I guess no but I do not have access to the code currently to verify this. Still I suspect this conditional test is useless.

It is indeed, from a mere compilation point of view. Because of a gitlab ci stage, clang-analyze is run against all changed files in the last commit, that fails because the lib is not present. This check is useful for that purpose only. I didn't find any better solution.

So this is clearly a clang / script defect that should not analyze the file like CMake does not try to compile it. This workaround should not be added IMHO. Is this clang analyzer result a mandatory step to merge the change or simply an extra check? I hope we don't have to pollute the code like this for every optional plugin...
I agree with you. But it's a mandatory step preventing the merge.
